experiment: Polymarket BTC 5-minute binaries: taker v1 vs passive makers
phase_rule: every maker quotes normally, goes reduce-only once its position could not be unwound in time (5x the time to trade it at 10% of the tape's volume), and rests what is left at the touch to close in the last 60 seconds

previous_phases.change: no aggro close; makers rested only where the edge curve allowed
previous_phases.result: The best scored maker (maker_model_100ms) beats the original taker by $+0.341 per window (95% CI $+0.022 to $+0.643).

previous_phases.change: aggro close at all times: any position rested at the touch to close
previous_phases.result: The best scored maker (maker_anchored_0ms) cannot yet be told apart from the original taker by $-0.074 per window (95% CI $-0.646 to $+0.455). Every maker tripped both kill criteria: negative PnL per window at 95% confidence after 200 windows, and a negative 5s markout.

headline: Collecting: 0 of 200 settled windows before any arm is scored. Numbers below are running totals, not results.

arms.name: taker_v1
arms.description: The original tool, unchanged: buys the ask when N(d2) beats ask + taker fee, polling REST every 3s.

arms.name: maker_mid
arms.description: Rests quotes around the Polymarket mid. No outside information -- measures what passive quoting alone is worth. Phase 3: quotes normally, goes reduce-only once its position could not be unwound in time (5x the time to trade it at 10% of the tape's volume), and rests what is left at the touch to close in the last 60 seconds.

kill_criteria: A maker arm whose mean PnL per window is below zero at 95% confidence after 200 settled windows is stopped.
A maker arm with a negative mean 5s markout after 500 fills is being picked off; stopped.
Written before the first paper fill (2026-09-25), carried unchanged into phase 2 (2026-10-30), and not moved after seeing results.
caveats: Every maker reads BTC as a spread-weighted Binance + OKX mid; the taker keeps its original Binance feed.

Phase 3 started from flat on 2026-11-04: every maker quotes normally, goes reduce-only once its position could not be unwound in time (5x the time to trade it at 10% of the tape's volume), and rests what is left at the touch to close in the last 60 seconds. Phases 1 and 2 are archived in the repo (archive/phase1/, archive/phase2/) with their raw records and are not mixed into these numbers.
Paper fills. A resting order joins the back of its price level, goes live 0.4s after it is sent, and fills only when a real print reaches it; a cancel takes 0.4s and can still be filled meanwhile.
Maker rebates are ignored and the taker pays the published fee, so the maker side is understated.
Only prints on the websocket move the paper queue; hidden or cross-matched liquidity is not modelled.
One process, one laptop: windows lost to sleep or a network drop are lost for every arm at once, and windows on declared downtime days (automation/downtime.json) are not scored.
